key_insight: DobicVLM improves chest X-ray report generation by combining supervised fine-tuning with GRPO and rule-based clinical rewards to better enforce structure, anatomy coverage, and semantic faithfulness.
clinical_relevance: It may help produce more clinically usable radiology reports in resource-limited settings by aligning outputs with explicit radiology standards rather than opaque neural reward models.
method: Started with supervised fine-tuning of MedGemma-4B on chest X-ray image-report pairs.
Applied Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) using programmatic rewards for structure, anatomy checklist, semantic similarity, and report length.
Used interpretable rule-based rewards instead of a neural reward model.
evidence_signal: The model was trained on 1,000 de-identified cases and evaluated on 69 held-out cases with blinded expert review, where it outperformed Gemini 2.5 Flash on most criteria.
watch_item: Results come from a relatively small private dataset, so broader validation is needed before real-world clinical deployment.
paper_title: DobicVLM: Aligning Chest X-Ray Report Generation with Clinically-Grounded Programmatic Rewards via Group Relative Policy Optimization
